← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Pan context and uncertainty — P4 baseline, P5 digital refinement

Owner scope clarification (2026-10-13): P5 continues with digital reconstruction and scenario-bounded virtual fitment; no physical measurement gate is required. The current proxy is an input to improve, not a verified pan model.

The reconstructed pan is a visual context for design exploration. It must not be used to manufacture a replacement pan or infer a measured Solstice fit.

Reference: official GM pan interior, official product. The retained exact-interface follow-up identifies the pan/cover/baffle screw family but supplies no metric hidden cavity or five-seat coordinates.

The official GM 12601240 interior photo provides qualitative exact-part topology but no calibrated internal coordinates. Vue service figures 1868082/1318093 are application-unresolved; figure 1866784 is an LY7/12666374 analog. See the source applicability assessment; none supplies pan, seat or pickup dimensions.

Full-pan cutaway images remove part of one side wall to expose the insert. Detail views additionally crop the shallow extension. Section models remove one half through X=0; this can hide side gates and is not an instruction to remove parts. Exploded views move the insert and cover vertically for explanation, without modelling a proven removal path or mounting connection. All numeric proxy inputs and geometry construction dimensions live in src/design_parameters.py; the register and generated summary are derivative views.

All render views use the same source placement. Grey is the assumed pan/cover context; purple is the assumed pickup/tube test envelope; blue/teal is custom structure and gold is the custom moving leaf. Real source photography remains separate from rendered concept geometry.

The P5 validator also checks four one-variable stress cases alongside the nominal proxy: cover underside −12 mm; pickup and tube diameters +25%; pickup and tube centerline +12/−8 mm in X/Y; and pan-interior scale −0.04 in X/Y. These are deliberately selected sensitivities, not confidence bounds. The exact A/B/C outcomes and tested poses are recorded in `review/digital-fit-scenario-assessment.md`. The Honda precedents in `research/honda-precedents.md` inform architectural comparisons, never these Solstice proxy dimensions.

Straight vertical withdrawal is sampled at 1 mm increments from the nominal closed-door placement, with the cover removed. A/B/C hit the rising tube proxy at 7 mm lift (4 mm in the 25%-larger tube case). If the complete pickup/tube proxy is omitted, the sampled path clears in four shell contexts; nested C begins in shell interference under the narrowed-shell case. Eight alternative routes per concept also test ±20 mm shifts along X/Y or ±5° tilts about X/Y before lifting. Translation uses 1 mm samples; rotation uses 1° samples around the insert bounding-box centre. All 24 selected routes meet the nominal tube or shell proxy, with first contacts at 10–13 mm of lateral shift, 2–3° of tilt, or during lift. These sampled first-hit results neither prove all possible paths are blocked nor establish a continuous/actual service path. The exact pickup/tube geometry and suction-pipe removal sequence remain unknown.
